messages:
maria: Heads-up — APAC edge saw a noisy-reschedule event during last night's preempt window, dedicated slices in ap-southeast-1 fragmented and we have cross-AZ egress spikes.
ashok: Saw that. Dashboard shows 4 dedicated pools lost >20% co-located slots after preempt, traffic routed to fallback pools in another AZ.
jules: Any pod-level OOMs or just routing churn? noticing KV cache regen on the affected GPUs.
maria: No OOMs, mostly KV cache warmups + reclaim churn. Latency tail jumped ~350ms for a subset of tenants.
devops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary drain started at 02:13 UTC for ap-southeast-1; 6/12 hosts drained for maintenance.
sam: Are those drains the preempt maintenance or the autoscaler balancing? I thought reserved capacity shouldn’t be drained mid-window.
ashok: It's a mix — host-level maintenance + cloud preemptible reclaiming. Our fractional-dedicated algorithm let some fractional slices move, causing undersized remaining slices.
lee: What’s the routing fallback? Are requests going to lower-memory model variants across AZs? That would explain egress spike.
maria: Yes — smart-router fell back to compatible variant in eu-west because local dedicated capacity depleted. That created cross-region egress and increased cost.
jules: Can we blink a flag to prefer same-AZ cold start instead of cross-region fallback for dedicated tenants? Even if slower, avoids egress and cost.
ashok: We have a policy knob: route_policy.prefer_local=true but it was overridden by slot_safety=false during the drain. I can revert for the affected pools.
sam: Reverting sounds good. Also can we lengthen preemptible grace window by 30s to reduce fragmentation? The quick churn is the killer.
maria: Agree — propose: 1) toggle prefer_local for dedicated tag 2) bump preempt_grace from 15s -> 45s for ap-southeast-1 preemptible hosts 3) throttle inter-AZ routing for dedicated tenants by 80%.
jules: Also add a KV cache warmup hint when moving slices so the router can prefer warm hosts if available.
lee: Cost note: cross-region fallback added ~0.12 USD per 1k tokens last night for a few high-embedding tenants. Need to log that to billing-alerts.
ashok: I'll flip prefer_local now on the canary pools in ap-southeast-1 and roll preempt_grace as an experiment.
maria: Thanks. Sam — can you open a short runbook snippet for oncall so they don’t repeatedly flip things? Something like:

```
If ap-southeast-1 resharding ->
 1) set route_policy.prefer_local=true for dedicated pools
 2) set preempt_grace=45s for preemptible hosts
 3) enable cache-warmup-hint for moved slices
 4) monitor egress-cost alert threshold 0.05USD/min
```

sam: On it. I'll add the snippet under runbooks/reshard-protection and ping #oncall.
devops-bot: monitor-bot: Egress cost alert fired: 2024-11-03T02:45:02Z for tenant:ml-payments. Spike +82% vs baseline.
jules: Can we schedule a dedicated warm pool prefill for heavy tenants after these events? Even a small warm pool reduces KV regen.
lee: Prefill = reserved slots; might cost more but better tail SLOs. Suggested plan: reserved warm pool 10% of committed capacity for 30m after reshard.
maria: For immediate mitigation, prefer_local + preempt_grace should dampen most of it. Longer term: prefill + better slot-placement heuristics.
ashok: Done — prefer_local flipped on canary. Rolling preempt_grace up next.
sam: Runbook PR created: https://internal/repo/runbooks/reshard-protection/ + pinged @oncall in #oncall
maria: Keep sharing telemetry. I'll follow up with cost delta and a proposal for an automated 'reshard-protect' policy.
jules: Thx everyone. If we still see >20% fragmentation after the experiment, we'll open a postmortem and consider AZ-locked dedicated pools.
lee: Quick ask — can we add a tiny label on tenant metrics when fallback occurs so billing shows fallback vs normal? Useful for chargeback.
ashok: Good idea, will add router.fallback_tag to telemetry events.
maria: Closing the loop: will post postmortem pointer + cost summary in 2 business days unless immediate issues recur. :thumbsup:
